question.prompt: Let \(N\) be the greatest five-digit number whose digits have a product of \(120.\) What is the sum of the digits of \(N?\)

solutions.explanation:
To make a five-digit number as large as possible, maximize its leftmost digit first, then the next digit, while preserving the required product.

No digit can be zero, and every digit must divide \(120\). The largest possible first digit is \(8\): it divides \(120\), while \(9\) does not. After choosing \(8\), the remaining four digits must have product \(120/8=15\).

The largest digit dividing \(15\) is \(5\), so choose it next. The remaining product is \(3\), giving next digit \(3\), followed by \(1,1\). These choices are feasible and produce the greatest number \(85311\).

Its digit sum is \(8+5+3+1+1=\boxed{18}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\). Comparing from left to right is what makes the successive largest feasible choices decisive.
solutions.title: Maximize feasible digits in left-to-right order
